title: RFK Jr.'s CDC isn’t letting states order COVID-19 shots for kids, blocking access
gist: The CDC under HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has not finalized procurement of 2026–27 COVID-19 vaccines through the Vaccines for Children program, which covers about 52% of US children, delaying access in states including 11 universal-purchase states. Leading medical groups led by the AAP still strongly urge vaccination for infants 6–23 months, diverging from CDC guidance.

insights.claim: The CDC has unexpectedly delayed letting states order seasonal COVID-19 vaccines through the Vaccines for Children program, which provides free vaccines to uninsured, underinsured, Medicaid-eligible and Indigenous children and covers about 52 percent of all US children.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Federal procurement is a major demand channel for pediatric COVID-19 vaccines; delays directly cut seasonal volumes for vaccine makers.

insights.claim: At least 11 states and one territory (Alaska, Connecticut, Hawaii, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Rhode Island, Vermont, Washington, Wyoming and American Samoa) buy all children's vaccines through VFC contracts, so the delay blocks access for all children there regardless of insurance.
